purpose: Newly shipping and overlooked local-AI hardware: one current 128GB Strix Halo system variant plus legacy NVIDIA cards whose memory topology materially affects LLM suitability.

hardware.storage: 2x M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4, RAID 0/1; vendor states up to 8TB total

power.note: Adapter rating is not wall-load consumption.

quantization_compatibility: GGUF Q4/Q5/Q8 via compatible CPU/Vulkan/ROCm runtimes
hardware.model_size_practicality: 128GB unified memory makes many 70B-class and selected 100B+ quantized models capacity-feasible; real generation speed remains bounded by roughly 256GB/s theoretical memory bandwidth and runtime maturity.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: moderate_to_good; processor can operate below its maximum cTDP, but the complete AC-powered system should be measured at the wall for deployment sizing.

vendor_benchmark_claims.claim: 2.2x faster inference than RTX 4090 in an LM Studio comparison at 13% power
vendor_benchmark_claims.caveat: The indexed product page does not expose enough model, quantization, context, or power-method detail for normalized comparison.

hardware.notes: System variant of the already-cataloged Ryzen AI Max+ 395 platform; do not count as a separate silicon architecture.

hardware.interconnect: NVLink; up to 200GB/s with two bridges, application support required for memory/performance scaling
software: CUDA 12.x-era toolchains for native Volta builds
PyTorch/llama.cpp support depends on versions built for sm_70
quantization_compatibility: GGUF CUDA quantizations where the runtime still targets sm_70
FP16/Tensor Core workloads on compatible CUDA 12.x-era software
hardware.model_size_practicality: 32GB HBM2 is suitable for many 20B-30B quantized models and selected larger models with offload; 870GB/s bandwidth is excellent for its age.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: poor_to_moderate; active cooling is easier than passive datacenter cards, but 250W board power is high.

pricing.note: Representative used marketplace asking price; seller/import provenance and warranty vary.

hardware.notes: CUDA 13 removed offline compilation and library support for Volta. CUDA 12.x remains the practical toolkit ceiling for building native Volta applications.

hardware.memory_topology: 4 independent GPUs x 8GB GDDR5; not a single 32GB memory pool
quantization_compatibility: small GGUF/CUDA models that fit inside one 8GB GPU, runtime/version dependent
hardware.model_size_practicality: Poor for a single large LLM despite the 32GB board total: each physical GPU has only 8GB. Multi-GPU runtimes may shard work, but the board should never be cataloged as a normal 32GB single-device accelerator.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: low; mainly educational/experimental or multi-service use because memory is split 4x8GB and Maxwell lacks Tensor Cores.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: poor; 225W board power plus required forced airflow for four small 8GB GPUs.

pricing.note: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia used listing; three units shown sold when indexed.

hardware.notes: Corrective record: the headline 32GB capacity is physically split across four GPUs. CUDA 13 removed offline compilation/library support for Maxwell, so CUDA 12.x is the practical native-build ceiling.
